source.title: Neural Networks Learning and Memorization with (almost) no Over-Parameterization

record.tranche_reason: The paper proves an SGD memorization result for random labeled points using a theoretical two-layer network setup, rather than reproducing the original experiments.
record.gate_note: Theorem 6 reports the paper's own random-label memorization result. Other memorization results cited from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Theorem 6 proves that SGD can fit arbitrarily close to all independently random binary labels, using a specially initialized two-layer network. This bears on V1 through a theoretical method.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's conclusion is accurate with conditions: SGD can perfectly memorize random labeled sphere points using a specially initialized two-layer network with Õ(m/d) hidden neurons and Õ(m) parameters, optimal up to polylogarithmic factors. Standard Xavier initialization and deeper networks remain open questions.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical result for depth two networks with Xavier initialization with zero outputs; the theorem chooses network width, initialization parameter B, learning rate η, and number of steps. It does not reproduce the original studies' experimental recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The theorem's guarantee is for random points on the sphere, a hinge loss, and chosen network and training parameters; it does not compare alternative settings.
record.problems: The result is a theoretical guarantee for a specific depth two setup and random points on the sphere. It does not measure test error, compare random labels with true labels, or establish the claim under unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
record.rows_left_out: No other qualifying study results on the claim were identified.

untested.parts: Standard initialization, deeper architectures, unchanged architecture and hyperparameters between true-label and random-label training, and measured test error.
Training-time comparison with true labels and convergence as the corrupted-label fraction increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs with the same networks.
Training and test errors across increasing fractions of label corruption.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on memorization and true-label generalization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before random labels.

record.verdict_notes: The special initialization restricts what the theorem establishes; it does not demonstrate that ordinary initialization fails. No limits_scope or challenges verdict follows from those untested settings.

versions.untested_parts: Test error at chance and fitting without changes to architecture or training hyperparameters are not tested. The result concerns random points on the sphere paired with random labels.

rows.subject: depth 2 neural network
rows.operation_detail: SGD memorization under Algorithm 1, with initialization and training parameters chosen for the theorem

conditions.value: m = d^c random, independent, uniform points in Sd−1 × {±1}, c > 1
any nonlinear and decent activation function

rows.measure: Fraction of examples memorized, where example i is memorized if yi h(xi) > 0
rows.value: 1 − ε fraction of the examples, with probability 1 − om(1)
rows.note: The theorem also specifies T = Õ(εm²) steps and allows a choice of B and η. It does not report test error or compare against training on true labels.
rows.check: Correct the width to q = Õ(m/d) hidden neuron pairs, giving Õ(m) parameters; it is not Õ(md). The iteration bound is T = Õ(m/ε²), whose fraction formatting is lost in the extraction. The guarantee permits arbitrarily small ε; Section 3.2 explicitly explains that ε < 1/m gives perfect memorization. Retain the special paired zero-output initialization and theorem-chosen training parameters as conditions.

relationships.condition: Independent uniform sphere inputs with independent random binary labels; two-layer networks with paired zero-output initialization and theorem-chosen SGD parameters.
relationships.reason: R1 guarantees memorization of a 1 − ε fraction with high probability; choosing ε < 1/m yields perfect training classification.
relationships.display_finding: With high probability, the network memorizes a 1−ε fraction of examples, yielding perfect training classification when ε < 1/m.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
